gaps.sentence: Don't forget ___ the plants while we're away.
gaps.explanation: forget + to-infinitive = fail to do something you should do.

gaps.sentence: I'm looking forward to ___ from you.
gaps.explanation: 'to' is a preposition in look forward to, so -ing follows: hearing.

gaps.sentence: You'd better ___ a taxi or you'll miss the plane.
gaps.explanation: had better takes the bare infinitive: you'd better take.

gaps.sentence: Do you want me ___ you at the station?
gaps.explanation: want + object + to-infinitive: want me to meet.

gaps.sentence: I didn't mean ___ you — it was a joke.
gaps.explanation: mean (= intend) takes the to-infinitive: didn't mean to upset. (mean + -ing = involve.)

gaps.sentence: He denied ___ the money, but nobody believed him.
They've postponed ___ the new bridge until spring.
